references.text: In [ref:Matt 26:20|Matthew 26:20], it is told that Jesus sat down with the twelve when evening had come, a parallel account to Luke's description of the meal.
[ref:Mark 14:17|Mark 14:17] is Mark's parallel account where Jesus comes with the twelve when evening had come, and they reclined at the table and ate.

In [ref:Luk 22:15-16|Luke 22:15-16], Jesus continues by saying that he has earnestly desired to eat this Passover meal with them before he suffers – this gives context to why it was important for him to sit down with the apostles.
[ref:Joh 13:1-2|John 13:1-2] also describes the beginning of the last meal, where Jesus is aware that his hour has come – parallel to Luke's expression "when the hour came" (ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡ ὥρα).
In [ref:Luk 6:13|Luke 6:13], Jesus called the twelve and gave them the name "apostles" (ἀποστόλους), the same word used in Luke 22:14 to designate those who sat down with him.

[ref:Joh 13:23-25|John 13:23-25] describes the fellowship at the table during the last meal, where one of the disciples was lying on Jesus' breast – an elaboration of how they reclined (ἀνέπεσεν) as Luke describes.

[ref:Luk 22:11-12|Luke 22:11-12] tells about the preparations for the Passover meal, where Jesus asks the disciples to arrange the large upper room – this gives the direct context for them now sitting down at the table in verse 14.
[ref:Matt 26:17-19|Matthew 26:17-19] describes the preparations for the Passover meal in Matthew, which is the background for the gathering at the table that Luke 22:14 depicts.

In [ref:Joh 17:1|John 17:1], Jesus lifts his eyes to heaven and says "The hour has come", which gives theological depth to Luke's expression "when the hour came" – it points to his suffering and glorification.
